faq.q: Where does the word month come from?
faq.a: It comes from the same old word as moon. Early months followed the Moon's cycle of about 29 and a half days.
asks: Why is it called a month?

faq.q: Why don't 12 Moon cycles fit a year?
faq.a: Twelve Moon cycles last about 354 days, which is 11 days short of the 365-day year. That is why lunar calendars, like the Islamic calendar, move through the seasons.
asks: Why is a lunar year shorter?

faq.q: Why does February have only 28 days?
faq.a: In the old Roman calendar, February was the last month of the year and got the days left over. It gets a 29th day in leap years.

faq.q: Did Augustus steal a day from February?
faq.a: August is named after the emperor Augustus, and July after Julius Caesar. But the story that Augustus took a day from February is most likely a myth.

faq.q: How can I remember how many days each month has?
faq.a: Use your knuckles: every month that lands on a knuckle has 31 days, and the dips have 30, except February. Or learn the rhyme that starts Thirty days has September.

facts: Twelve lunar months last about 354 days, 11 days fewer than a solar year.
July is named after Julius Caesar and August after the emperor Augustus.
